questions.text: Which capabilities does psql provide? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Interactive execution of SQL queries
Executing commands from files
Using psql's own meta-commands
Automatically initializing a new PostgreSQL cluster on every startup

questions.explanation: psql is PostgreSQL's terminal client. It can execute queries interactively, read commands from files or command-line arguments, and provides its own meta-commands.

questions.text: Which psql invocation specifies database appdb, user dba, server db01, and port 5433?

answers.text: psql -d appdb -U dba -h db01 -p 5433
psql -U appdb -d dba -p db01 -h 5433
psql -h appdb -p dba -d db01 -U 5433
psql -p appdb -h dba -U db01 -d 5433

questions.explanation: In psql, -d specifies the database, -U the user, -h the host, and -p the server port.

questions.text: Which values does psql use by default if the corresponding connection parameters are not specified explicitly? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The database user name matches the operating-system user name
The default database name matches the resolved database user name
The database name is always postgres regardless of the user
The database user is always postgres

questions.explanation: If no user is specified, psql uses the operating-system user name by default. After the user has been determined, that name is also used as the default database name.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — psql, “Connecting to a Database” section

questions.text: You are already inside psql. Which command shows information about the current connection?

answers.text: \connect
\conninfo
\help
\list

questions.explanation: The \conninfo command displays information about the current connection. The \connect command establishes a new connection.

questions.text: Which mappings between help commands and their purposes are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: \? — list and short description of psql commands
\? variables — help for psql variables
\h — help for SQL commands
\q — display the syntax of an SQL command

questions.explanation: In psql, \? shows help for meta-commands, \? variables shows help for psql variables, and \h or \help shows help for SQL commands. \q exits psql.

questions.text: What does the psql -c option do?

answers.text: Passes the specified command to psql for execution
Specifies the PostgreSQL configuration directory
Always opens a new interactive connection after executing the command
Enables only expanded display mode for results

questions.explanation: The -c, or --command, option passes a command to psql for execution. When -c or -f is used, psql exits after processing the specified commands instead of reading commands from standard input.

questions.text: Which statements about the psql -f option are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: It reads commands from the specified file
It can be combined with the -c option
Its purpose is largely equivalent to the \i meta-command
After processing the file, psql always continues reading commands from standard input

questions.explanation: The -f option reads commands from a file, can be repeated and combined with -c, and is essentially similar to the \i meta-command. When -c or -f is present, psql exits after processing those options.

questions.text: How does psql distinguish its own meta-command from an ordinary SQL command?

answers.text: A meta-command starts with a backslash
A meta-command always starts with two hyphens
A meta-command must end with a colon
A meta-command is enclosed in square brackets

questions.explanation: Psql's own commands begin with a backslash. They are processed by psql itself rather than sent to the server as SQL.

source.locator: Slide 5 “Getting Help”; PostgreSQL 16 documentation — psql, “Meta-Commands” section

questions.text: Which statements about entering SQL in interactive psql are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A semicolon normally terminates an SQL command and sends it to the server
A normal newline does not by itself have to terminate an SQL command
An SQL command can be entered across multiple lines
Any command beginning with a backslash is sent to the server as SQL

questions.explanation: In normal mode, psql sends an SQL command to the server after the terminating semicolon. A newline does not necessarily terminate a statement, so SQL can be entered on multiple lines. Backslash meta-commands are processed by psql itself.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — psql, “Entering SQL Commands” and “Meta-Commands” sections

questions.text: Which mappings between libpq environment variables and connection parameters are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: PGHOST — host
PGDATABASE — dbname
PGPORT — user
PGUSER — port

questions.explanation: PGHOST corresponds to host, PGDATABASE to dbname, PGPORT to port, and PGUSER to user. These variables can supply default connection parameters.

questions.text: Which password storage method is safer to use instead of the PGPASSWORD environment variable?

answers.text: The .pgpass password file
The PGPORT variable
The PROMPT1 variable
The postgresql.conf file

questions.explanation: Using PGPASSWORD is not recommended for security reasons because on some systems process environment variables may be visible to other users. The documentation recommends using a password file instead.

questions.text: Which format corresponds to an entry in the.pgpass file?

answers.text: host_name:port:database:user_name:password
user_name:password:host_name:database
database=user_name=password=port
host_name;database;password

questions.explanation: A password-file line has five fields in this order: host name, port, database, user name, and password.

questions.text: Which rules for processing.pgpass entries are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The first four fields can use * to match any value
The password from the first matching line is used
The characters : and \ inside a value are escaped with a backslash when necessary
If several lines match, the last one is always selected

questions.explanation: The first four fields in .pgpass can contain the * wildcard, and lookup stops at the first matching entry. More specific entries should therefore be placed earlier when wildcards are used. Colons and backslashes are escaped.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — Section 34.16 “The Password File”, format and entry selection

questions.text: What happens on Unix if ~/.pgpass is accessible to group or other users?

answers.text: The file is ignored
psql automatically fixes the permissions
The file is used only for local connections
psql removes passwords from the file

questions.explanation: On Unix, the password file must deny access to group and other users. The documentation gives mode 0600 as an appropriate setting. With less restrictive permissions, the file is ignored.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — Section 34.16 “The Password File”, permissions

questions.text: Which statements about pg_service.conf are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The file maps a set of connection parameters to a service name
The service name can be specified through PGSERVICE
The file uses an INI-like format in which the section name is the service name
Changing service parameters requires recompiling the client application

questions.explanation: The connection service file maps a service name to connection parameters. A service can be selected through PGSERVICE, and the file uses INI format. One purpose is to allow connection parameters to be changed without recompiling the application.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — Section 34.17 “The Connection Service File”

questions.text: The same connection parameter is set in an environment variable, pg_service.conf, and directly in the connection string. Which value has the highest priority?

answers.text: The value specified directly in the connection string
The value from the environment variable
The value from pg_service.conf always has absolute priority
One of the three values is selected randomly

questions.explanation: A parameter from a service file overrides the corresponding environment variable, but can itself be overridden by a value specified directly in the connection string.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — Section 34.17 “The Connection Service File”, parameter merging

questions.text: Which statements about psql prompt variables are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: PROMPT1 defines the normal prompt when waiting for a new command
PROMPT2 is used when psql is waiting for continuation of an unfinished command
PROMPT1 sets the user's connection password
PROMPT2 selects the pager program

questions.explanation: PROMPT1 controls the primary psql prompt. PROMPT2 is displayed for continuation input, for example when a command has not yet been terminated with a semicolon or quotes remain open.

questions.text: Which psql command enables display of the execution time of each SQL statement?

answers.text: \timing on
\time start
\profile on
\duration enable

questions.explanation: The \timing on meta-command enables display of the execution time of each SQL statement. Calling \timing without an argument toggles the current state.

questions.text: Which statements about paging psql output are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The pager program can be set through PSQL_PAGER
Pager behavior can be controlled through \pset
If both PSQL_PAGER and PAGER are set, PSQL_PAGER is considered first
psql always uses a pager even if it is explicitly disabled

questions.explanation: psql supports the PSQL_PAGER and PAGER variables and the \pset pager setting. PSQL_PAGER has priority over PAGER. The pager can be disabled.

source.locator: PostgreSQL 16 documentation — psql, PSQL_PAGER/PAGER and \pset pager

questions.text: Which psql command displays a detailed list of databases?

answers.text: \conninfo+

questions.explanation: In the practical part of the material, \l+ is suggested for displaying a detailed list of databases.

questions.text: Which statements about the .psqlrc file and psql settings are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: .psqlrc can contain settings that should be applied on subsequent psql startups
\setenv in .psqlrc can set PSQL_PAGER only for psql sessions
The -X option starts psql without reading psqlrc startup files
.psqlrc is a server configuration file read by the postgres process

questions.explanation: In the practical part, .psqlrc is used for persistent user-level psql settings, including through \setenv. The -X, or --no-psqlrc, option prevents reading the system and user psql startup files.

source.locator: Slide 8 “Practice” and PostgreSQL 16 documentation — psql, -X/--no-psqlrc option

questions.text: What does ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK=on do inside a transaction block? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: psql implicitly creates a SAVEPOINT before each command
On error, psql rolls back to the created savepoint
After an error, the transaction can continue
Every successful command automatically ends the transaction with COMMIT

questions.explanation: With ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK=on, psql establishes an implicit savepoint before every command in a transaction block. If a command fails, psql rolls back to that savepoint, allowing the transaction to continue.

source.locator: Slide 9 “Practice+”; PostgreSQL 16 documentation — psql, ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK variable

questions.text: How does ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK=interactive differ from ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK=on?

answers.text: Rollback after an error applies only in interactive sessions, not while reading scripts
Rollback applies only while executing scripts
Any error immediately terminates psql
The interactive value completely disables savepoints

questions.explanation: The interactive value enables the described behavior only for interactive psql sessions. It does not apply when commands are being executed from scripts.

questions.text: Which statements about the psql -1/--single-transaction option are true? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: It is used together with one or more -c and/or -f options
psql executes BEGIN before the first processed command and COMMIT after the last
With an error and ON_ERROR_STOP, ROLLBACK is executed instead of COMMIT
It is intended only to change the appearance of the psql prompt

questions.explanation: The --single-transaction option wraps commands supplied through -c and -f in one transaction. With ON_ERROR_STOP enabled, an error causes a ROLLBACK instead of the final COMMIT.
